question: Does TensorLBM's Peskin tensor-product immersed-boundary stencil + multi-pass direct forcing reproduce haimingz/vivsim's tensor-product stencil + multi-direct forcing (MDF) within the owner 15% bar, and if not, which sub-operator is responsible?
decision: Ship the diff list + porting recommendation; if the operator differs by >15%, add a round-trip-consistent MDF forcing to TensorLBM and verify it against the OSS reference to <1e-2.

alternatives.A2_oss_mdf: haimingz/vivsim vivsim/ib/mdf.py multi_direct_forcing on vivsim/ib/stencil.py get_ib_stencil (vendored, numpy-shimmed, bodies byte-identical)
alternatives.A3_tensorlbm_mdf_port: direct_forcing_mdf added in this mission -- same Richardson scheme on IBMStencil (round-trip consistent)

hypothesis.H0: the two implementations agree to <15% on marker force and on the achieved interface condition at typical marker spacings (0.5-1.2 cells)
hypothesis.H1: the TensorLBM pointwise arm deviates by >15% because its fixed point f = 2 rho (U_t - u_int) omits the round-trip operator A = interp.spread whose row sum is ~0.4 at 1-cell spacing

metrics.stencil_max_abs_weight_diff: max |w_TL - w_OSS| after decoding both stencils to physical node coordinates (dimensionless)
metrics.stencil_node_keys_identical: boolean: the set of non-zero-support nodes per marker is the same
metrics.force_rel_vs_oss_converged: |sum_x F_grid(arm) - sum_x F_grid(OSS, n_iter=40)| / |sum_x F_grid(OSS, n_iter=40)|
metrics.iface_slip_rel: max_k |U_target - (u_int + 0.5 * interp(spread(F)))| / U_inf  (the no-slip the operator actually achieves)
metrics.A_row_sum_mean: mean over markers of sum_n w_k(n) * sum_k' w_k'(n), the row sum of the round-trip operator
metrics.measured_amplification: sum_x F_grid(OSS converged) / sum_x F_grid(pointwise converged)
metrics.cd_mean_last_half: mean C_D over the second half of the run, C_D = -sum_k F_kx / (0.5 rho U^2 D) (end-to-end, relative comparison only)

unit_of_analysis: one operator evaluation at fixed (marker set, grid, velocity field); end-to-end: one completed LBM run per (Re, arm)

baseline_control.primary_control: A2 (OSS MDF) -- the mature implementation named by the anchor; identical marker coordinates, identical Eulerian field, identical kernel
baseline_control.exactness_control: TensorLBM loop-form ibm_velocity_interpolate / ibm_force_spread (an independent brute-force implementation) is used to validate that the numpy shim reproduces the OSS bodies: agreement must be < 1e-14
baseline_control.physical_reference: CYLINDER_CD_2D table already in the repo (src/tensorlbm/ibm_openwater.py:130, Dennis & Chang 1970) -- used only for the end-to-end informational column

predeclared_thresholds.stencil_identity: 1e-12 absolute on weights, identical non-zero node keys, 2-D and 3-D
predeclared_thresholds.oss_vs_tl_force: 15% relative on sum_x F_grid at matched convergence (n_iter = 10) and h = 0.9 cells
predeclared_thresholds.iface_slip: 15% relative interface slip; a PASS requires the slip below the bar, not merely a small arm-to-arm difference
predeclared_thresholds.end_to_end: 15% on Cd between arms (literature is an informational column, the setup is not claimed to be unbounded-flow accurate)

stopping_rule: all iteration counts and marker spacings are fixed in this file before the run; the operator levels stop after the predeclared sweep (n=1..40, h=0.5..3.0). No arm is extended or re-tuned after seeing a favourable number. End-to-end runs are fixed at 400 steps for the timing probe / 800 steps for the arm comparison, and are reported as relative-only because 800 steps is not a converged steady state.
variables_held_fixed: single marker set per h, one deterministic construction
confounders: the numpy shim runs float64 while upstream JAX defaults to float32 -- dtype is not reproduced (both arms float64, so the operator comparison is unaffected)
OSS marker_ds preconditions the MDF iteration; it changes the convergence path, not the converged force (measured: <2e-3, entry ds_preconditioner_only)
marker positions are identical across arms, so stencil overlap (cross-talk) is not a confounder but is the mechanism under test
the end-to-end run uses TensorLBM's own LBM for every arm (including the OSS arm), so only the IBM operator differs; the shared interior penalty is a known limitation of that driver
analysis: no outlier removal; relative errors against the OSS arm; convergence is reported as a separate table; the end-to-end column is reported arm-to-arm and flagged if the absolute Cd is not physically plausible
fail_stage_plan: fail_stage = L1_stencil / L2_mdf / L3_port / L4_end_to_end, failure_reason carries the measured deviation; partial results are kept, never overwritten
